claim: An operator comparison favors ntfy over Gotify for cross-server topics, ACLs and emoji, but criticizes ntfy's CLI-only user/permission configuration; Gotify is simpler but has limited user access controls.
quote: having access to topics from different servers, ACL or be able to add emojis to the messages ... The needs for CLI to configure users and permissions is not really convenient

claim: Apprise is positioned as a universal notification library/abstraction layer (110+ services) rather than a standalone server like ntfy or Gotify, valued as middleware glue.
quote: Instead of needing to integrate and maintain separate code for each notification channel, I just need to learn Apprise's simple and unified API ... supports 110+ different notification services

claim: Gotify's main weaknesses are message to only one destination user and no native secure iOS path (workarounds like igotify deemed insecure by default), while ntfy's weaknesses are no web admin and access-control that is not easy.
quote: Message only to one destination user ... iPhone & iPad – need igotify – igotify insecure by default, need self-host ntfy to more secure ... [ntfy] web admin does not exist ... Access-control not easy

claim: Philipp C. Heckel confirms he is essentially the sole maintainer of ntfy running it as a side project on a single DigitalOcean droplet, with modest revenue and an explicit choice not to depend on it financially — a single bus-factor.
quote: It's one box. It's one droplet on Digital Ocean ... ntfy makes a little bit of money. I'm not swimming in money, and that's okay ... I can't quit my day job because of it... Sadly ... I do like that it's entirely open, and that I don't depend financially on it

claim: Gotify's maintainer Jannis Mattheis (jmattheis) develops and maintains the project in his free time alongside a full-time job, indicating a similar single-maintainer bus-factor and modest, spaced-out release cadence.
quote: jmattheis creates and maintains Gotify projects in his free time besides his full time job

claim: Gotify has no official iOS app; operators rely on third-party bridge/workaround projects to deliver Gotify notifications to iPhones.
quote: There is no iOS app for Gotify (yet) ... a containerized solution as a workaround ... a Docker-based bridge that connects to your Gotify server and pushes messages to configured backends to enable iOS notifications
